lead.headline: Tennessee fails to execute Christa Pike after two lethal doses
lead.dek: Gov. Bill Lee halts the state's remaining 2026 execution and orders an outside review of what went wrong
body: Tennessee failed to execute Christa Pike in Nashville on Wednesday night after two doses of pentobarbital left the 50-year-old breathing and audibly snoring for more than 40 minutes, and she was taken to a hospital, her lawyers told a federal court.

Media witnesses at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution said the chamber blinds closed about 8:06 p.m. and they were ordered out at 8:53 p.m. with Pike still conscious. Witnesses said she told officials her arm felt "like it's about to burst open" and asked if it was supposed to feel that way. Her lawyers told the court she "still has a heartbeat."

Lee halted the state's remaining 2026 execution and ordered "a comprehensive, third-party review." The Department of Correction said it followed every step of its protocol. The Supreme Court had cleared the execution earlier Wednesday over three dissents. Pike, 50, was convicted in 1996 of murdering Colleen Slemmer, 19, in Knoxville.

briefs.headline: Hegseth orders 20% cut to generals and admirals by Jan. 1
briefs.summary: In a Quantico address Wednesday, the defense secretary doubled last year's 10% cut to the roughly 800 flag-officer posts and announced a four-star drone command.

briefs.headline: Trump announces $54B Korean stake in Alaska gas pipeline
briefs.summary: The White House said the pipeline is part of a $200B package that also covers eight nuclear plants and a Texas power plant. Sen. Dan Sullivan joined Trump Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Senate confirms Sonderling as labor secretary, 47-41
briefs.summary: The party-line vote Wednesday fills a post vacant since Lori Chavez-DeRemer left in April. It was the Senate's last business before it left for the midterm campaign.

briefs.headline: Senate Democrats block Husted data center rate bill, 57-43
briefs.summary: The Ratepayer Protection Act, which passed the House 417-3, fell short of 60 votes Wednesday. Schumer called it 'toothless'; Husted faces Sherrod Brown in November.

briefs.headline: Flydubai halts Israel flights after co-pilot stabs captain
briefs.summary: Netanyahu said a co-pilot stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar and tried to crash the jet, which dived before landing in Tabuk Wednesday; Saudi police held the pilot, and the 174 passengers reached Tel Aviv.

briefs.headline: Pakistan strikes Afghanistan; Kabul says 9 civilians dead
briefs.summary: Pakistan said overnight strikes in Kunar and Helmand killed 22 militants. The Taliban government said nine women and children died and 11 were wounded.

briefs.headline: France detains 625 as school protests spread nationwide
briefs.summary: Police detained 625 people Wednesday and 83 officers were wounded as student protests over timetables, class sizes and teacher shortages hit 356 schools.

briefs.headline: Puntland says pirates killed five crew on hijacked tanker
briefs.summary: Puntland's information ministry said pirates killed three Pakistanis, an Indian and a Myanmar national on the Palau-flagged Honour 25 before a rescue that seized 16 suspects.

briefs.headline: West Virginia withdraws from federal nuclear hub competition
briefs.summary: The state sent a one-paragraph letter pulling out of the DOE's nuclear campus program after days of dispute over handling nuclear waste, MetroNews reported.

briefs.headline: Capito announces bipartisan Senate deal on permitting reform
briefs.summary: Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich outlined the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act Wednesday after Democrats balked last week; a vote is next.

briefs.headline: Sample ballots go online for all 55 counties, Warner says
briefs.summary: Secretary of State Kris Warner's lookup tool shows each county's November ballot, including a constitutional amendment question, WVVA reported Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Barboursville man charged with 30 counts after fires, gunfire
briefs.summary: State Police say Joseph Daniels, 49, fired into the house Tuesday and set fires that destroyed it, three vehicles and an outbuilding; bail is $250,000.

regional.item: Seven more Fifth Avenue rentals tied to last month's Marshall evictions were never registered, with fines up to $18,000, WSAZ reported.
Two Parkersburg officers shot and killed a man who aimed a long gun at them on 11th Avenue about 9:20 p.m. Wednesday; State Police are investigating.
Julia Surbaugh's attorney told a judge Sept. 23 her amended habeas petition could be filed within two months, the Echo reported Tuesday.
Summers County Commission opens applications today for a deputy sheriff civil service exam, due Oct. 16 at 3 p.m., the Hinton News said.

away.item: A study for Bennington, Pownal, Woodford and Shaftsbury recommends merging the two rescue squads into one EMS district, the Banner said Wednesday.

hotspots.item: Cowen volunteer firefighters told Secretary of State Kris Warner during a recent visit that their station is too tight to fit the trucks, the Echo reported Tuesday.
Topsail Beach broke ground Sept. 24 on a $9.6M, 17,400-square-foot public safety building on Flake Avenue to house its police and fire departments.

briefs.headline: Hundreds mark reconciliation day at Lheidli T'enneh park
briefs.summary: A guided walk and a reading of the 94 calls to action opened Wednesday's gathering in Prince George. Chief Dolleen Logan said the day is for every walk of life.

briefs.headline: Pickup hits reconciliation walk in Delta, killing two elders
briefs.summary: A pickup hit four people outside Tsawwassen Mills in Delta Wednesday as the First Nation marked the day; police said the driver may have had a medical emergency.

briefs.headline: Smaller B.C. parties lag as Oct. 3 nomination deadline nears
briefs.summary: Elections BC listed 43 official NDP and 32 Conservative candidates as of Sept. 30 for 93 ridings; CentreBC and OneBC had one each and the Greens seven.

briefs.headline: Carney set to name West Coast pipeline a national-interest project
briefs.summary: The prime minister is expected in Fort McMurray with Premier Danielle Smith today, the Oct. 1 deadline set in the May implementation deal. It would be the first designation under Bill C-5.

briefs.headline: Conservative MP Aitchison says he will resign at end of fall sitting
briefs.summary: The Parry Sound-Muskoka MP and 2022 leadership candidate said Wednesday he is leaving after 30 years in public life. He has been the party's housing critic.

briefs.headline: NASA, SpaceX poll go for Crew-13 launch at 11:10 a.m. today
briefs.summary: Managers cleared the Launch Readiness Review Wednesday for a Falcon 9 liftoff from Cape Canaveral; forecasters cut weather odds to 55% favorable.

briefs.headline: Swiss glaciers lose a fifth of their ice in five years
briefs.summary: The GLAMOS monitoring network said 5.5% of volume melted in 2026, the second-worst year on record, after the hottest summer since 1864.

briefs.headline: Astronauts on long missions break hips younger, study finds
briefs.summary: A Mayo Clinic Proceedings review of U.S. astronauts' annual exams found higher hip fracture rates after flights over 90 days and urges CT bone scans.

briefs.headline: Cannabis users twice as likely to commit violence, review finds
briefs.summary: A King's College London meta-analysis of 63 studies and 265,000 people found the link strongest in psychiatric patients; authors say causation is unproven.

briefs.headline: Newsom signs SB 947 requiring humans to review AI job decisions
briefs.summary: The governor signed 13 AI bills Wednesday, including SB 951 requiring notice when AI causes mass layoffs and two on AI in clinical care. No vetoes were listed.

briefs.headline: Reddit ends RSS feeds and public API, citing AI scrapers
briefs.summary: RSS stops Nov. 13 and public API access ends in March 2027; Reddit said both had become surfaces for large-scale scraping. AI tools will need paid deals.

briefs.headline: Meta denies its Muse agent read a user's private messages
briefs.summary: Inc. columnist Jason Aten said Muse for Mac read his Messages with disk access off. Meta's Andy Stone said the feature is opt-in and needs three permissions.

weather_ear: Thursday's sky and temperature come from Jim Claudtore at 7:15.
kicker: Putnam-Kanawha's line was held for space; Crew-13 is set for 11:10 a.m., Carney's pipeline decision is due today, and the Browns host the Steelers at 8:15.
